title: Global Viral Lower Respiratory Disease Episodes, Hospitalisations, and Clinical Outcomes by Aetiology, 2010-2021.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Viral lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) is a major global cause of morbidity and mortality, yet pathogen-specific burden estimates remain limited, creating uncertainty for policy and clinical practice. The study aimed to quantify the global burden of viral LRTD episodes, hospitalisations, and severe clinical outcomes by aetiology from 2010 to 2021.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 modelling framework to generate estimates for 204 countries and territories, 21 regions, and seven super-regions from 2010 to 2021. Data inputs included surveillance systems, clinical informatics, published literature, surveys, and vital registration.
analysis.methods: Viral LRTD incidence was estimated using DisMod-MR 2.1, a GBD Bayesian meta-regression tool, and hospitalisations were derived using location-specific admission scalars adjusted for healthcare access. Aetiology-specific clinical outcome proportions, including ICU need, IMV need, and in-hospital mortality, were estimated using meta-regression-Bayesian, regularised, trimming models and applied to hospitalisation estimates.
analysis.main_results: Globally, viral LRTD episodes increased from 82.3 million (95% UI 76.4–88.2) in 2010 to 94.9 million (88.8–101.2) in 2019, while episode rates remained stable at approximately 1200 per 100,000 population. Between 2010 and 2019, global rates of ICU need increased from 16.1 (14.3–18.0) to 23.7 (21.0–26.6) per 100,000, IMV need from 7.5 (6.7–8.4) to 11.2 (10.0–12.6), and in-hospital mortality from 9.4 (8.4–10.5) to 13.9 (12.3–15.6) per 100,000.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Before 2020, global incidence of viral LRTD was stable, but hospitalisations and severe outcomes increased substantially, indicating rising clinical severity and healthcare demand. The study provides the first comprehensive, aetiology-specific global burden estimates for viral LRTD over a decade, highlighting marked age and regional variations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings underscore the substantial burden of severe viral LRTD globally, particularly among older adults, and reveal pronounced regional disparities. The results support the need for sustained aetiology-specific surveillance, adequate healthcare capacity, and equitable access to preventive and therapeutic interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on modelled estimates rather than primary data, which may introduce uncertainty and limit generalisability to specific settings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of direct measurements and potential biases in data inputs and modelling assumptions.

analysis.summary_en: This study quantified the global burden of viral lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) by aetiology from 2010 to 2021 using the GBD 2021 framework. It estimated episodes, hospitalisations, and severe outcomes for five viral categories, including human metapneumovirus (hMPV), across 204 countries. Between 2010 and 2019, viral LRTD episodes rose from 82.3 million to 94.9 million, while hospitalisation and severe outcome rates increased substantially, particularly among older adults. The COVID-19 pandemic in 2020–2021 dramatically altered the landscape, with SARS-CoV-2 driving unprecedented increases in hospitalisations and mortality while suppressing other respiratory viruses. The findings highlight the need for sustained surveillance, healthcare capacity, and equitable access to interventions, though the evidence is limited by reliance on modelled estimates and potential biases.

title: Optimization of the antiviral spectrum of cyclophilin inhibitors targeting respiratory viruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the antiviral activity of a library of urea-based small-molecule cyclophilin inhibitors against human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), addressing the need for broad-spectrum antiviral agents targeting respiratory viruses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research involved in vitro testing of 36 cyclophilin inhibitors against hRSV and hMPV, with subsequent optimization of dual-acting derivatives and evaluation in immortalized cell lines and fully differentiated human nasal epithelial cells.
analysis.methods: Structure–spectrum analysis and structure–activity relationship-guided optimization were employed to design and test optimized compounds, with competition assays using alisporivir to confirm the mechanism of action.
analysis.main_results: The optimized compound F832/33 demonstrated potent, broad-spectrum antiviral activity with nanomolar efficacy against hRSV and hMPV, submicromolar inhibition of cyclophilin PPIase activity, no cytotoxicity, and additional activity against parainfluenza virus type 3, enterovirus D68, and SARS-CoV-2 strains.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that cyclophilin engagement rather than enzymatic inhibition is required for antiviral activity, and structure–activity relationship-guided optimization successfully expanded the antiviral spectrum of cyclophilin inhibitors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: F832/33 is positioned as a promising host-targeted broad-spectrum antiviral candidate with potential implications for treating and preventing infections caused by multiple respiratory pathogens.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vitro studies, and further in vivo research is needed to evaluate therapeutic potential and clarify the precise mechanism of action; however, the robust in vitro results support a moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the antiviral activity of 36 urea-based cyclophilin inhibitors against hRSV and hMPV, leading to the rational design of optimized dual-acting derivatives. The compound F832/33 emerged as a potent, broad-spectrum agent with nanomolar activity against both viruses, additional efficacy against other respiratory pathogens, and no cytotoxicity. The results revealed that cyclophilin engagement, not enzymatic inhibition, drives antiviral effects, and structure–activity optimization successfully expanded the antiviral spectrum. F832/33 represents a promising host-targeted candidate, though further in vivo studies are needed to confirm therapeutic potential and mechanism.

title: Comparative evaluation of classical and machine learning methods for medical image enhancement

analysis.research_question_and_background: Medical imaging is critical for diagnostic accuracy, yet raw images often suffer from noise and low contrast, necessitating effective enhancement techniques.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study provides a comparative evaluation of classical methods, namely the Laplace transform (LT), Sobel operator (SO), and histogram equalization (HE), against a data-driven convolutional neural network (CNN) using the musculoskeletal radiographs (MURA) and Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) lung computed tomography (CT) datasets.
analysis.methods: The supplied evidence does not report detailed sampling, assay, or statistical analysis procedures beyond the general comparative framework.
analysis.main_results: Quantitative analysis shows that HE and SO significantly outperform other methods in isolated contrast enhancement and edge definition, whereas the CNN based approach demonstrates superior detail preservation and entropy.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that although classical operators remain highly effective for specific boundary detection tasks, machine learning frameworks provide the most robust performance for cross-modality image enhancement.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that machine learning frameworks offer a more balanced and adaptive solution for diverse diagnostic requirements, bridging the gap between raw data acquisition and clinical interpretation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate because the provided text lacks detailed methodology, sample size specifics, and statistical parameters, while noting that classical methods often introduce artifacts.

analysis.summary_en: This study compared classical image enhancement methods—Laplace transform, Sobel operator, and histogram equalization—against a convolutional neural network using MURA and HMPV lung CT datasets. While histogram equalization and the Sobel operator excelled in specific metrics like contrast and edge definition, they often introduced artifacts. In contrast, the convolutional neural network demonstrated superior detail preservation and entropy. The authors concluded that although classical operators are effective for boundary detection, machine learning frameworks provide more robust performance for cross-modality enhancement, offering adaptive solutions for clinical diagnostics.

title: Epidemiology, Clinical Characteristics, and Severity of Human Parainfluenza Virus Infection in Children from 2015-2025: A Scoping Review Protocol

analysis.scope_and_question: This scoping review aims to map evidence on the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and severity of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) infection in hospitalised children from 2015-2025, comparing HMPV serotypes and other respiratory viruses, and identifying risk factors for severe outcomes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review will include studies on HMPV infection in children, comparing different serotypes and other respiratory viruses, and identifying risk factors for severe outcomes. The review will follow a scoping review methodology, including a systematic search of relevant databases and a narrative synthesis of the included studies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review will provide evidence on the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and severity of HMPV infection in children, as well as comparisons between HMPV serotypes and other respiratory viruses, and risk factors for severe outcomes.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review may identify controversies and evidence gaps in the current understanding of HMPV infection in children, such as the role of different serotypes in disease severity and the effectiveness of current diagnostic and treatment strategies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review will inform future research and clinical practice by identifying areas for further study and highlighting the need for improved diagnostic and treatment strategies for HMPV infection in children.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review protocol outlines a plan to map the available evidence on the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and severity of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) infection in hospitalised children from 2015-2025. The review aims to compare different HMPV serotypes, other common respiratory viruses, and risk factors for severe outcomes. The review will follow a systematic search and narrative synthesis methodology, providing evidence to inform future research and clinical practice. The review may also identify controversies and evidence gaps in the current understanding of HMPV infection in children.
